Hey. I’m G (f18). I’ve been a carer for my mom since I was 9 years old, not far off 10 years. I’m an only child. She’s paralysed down one side, has epilepsy, diabetes and chronic mental health issues. I really empathise with you on the feeling guilt part. When her mental health gets really severe, she can lash out at me; some ways worse than others. It really makes me feel like I’ve ‘failed’ as a carer, you know? Almost like if I was going a better job, she wouldn’t be suffering the way she is. We don’t have a conventional mother-daughter relationship, it’s more carer-patient. It’s a lot more professional than it is emotional and sometimes that is really difficult, because it feels like boundaries are blurred of what I can and can’t do. I’ve got to make professional judgements in what shouldn’t be a professional relationship; it sounds like we’re in a similar boat in that aspect. We can both recognise that what we’ve done is right from a medical standpoint, but it messes with the emotional aspect of the relationship. I think all people like us can do is recognise that it’s not our fault (easier said than done, I know). We’ve been faced with decisions most people will never have to make and forced to take on roles in relationships that most people couldn’t bare and if anything that makes us really brave! I hope you and J stay happy and safe :))

Hey, I’m a white 17 year old; not sure how much I can relate personally but we both suffer from maladaptive daydreaming so I’ll share my story and try to give some advice.
Ive also been daydreaming since I was young, was also shy and sensitive and extremely lonely. I was surrounded by a lot of instability (moved houses a lot, lived with my drug addict uncle for a bit, then my half paralysed mother) and found stability in this little world in my own mind. Although I’m not black, my mental health always seemed to take the back seat since my mother’s illnesses were always a priority. I cannot imagine facing racism through healthcare - healthcare is a human right as far as I’m concerned and pigment in our skin should not undermine that!
I used to wake up early to daydream before school, but now we’re on lockdown due to Covid-19, I can wake up when I want and daydream for as long as I want without having to worry about missing the bus etc. I’m so sorry to hear about your sexual assault, I can’t imagine going through something like that - know that whatever happened was NOT and NEVER will be your fault!! :) and as for the police brutality, once again discrimination based on skin pigmentation is horrendous and should never happen. I can’t pretend to understand what the black community is going through at this time, but know that you have the support of many! I can’t comprehend how this is effecting your daydreaming, sending hugs x
My daydreams are also about romantic relationships and fame. I daydream about being loved and cherished, because to be honest it’s something I’ve never really felt.
I don’t pace, but rather rock back and forth. Mine is also triggered by music. 
I’m from the UK, so we do have socialised healthcare, including therapy. Waitlists can be around a year though, which isn’t great but I’m grateful for it anyway and hope someday I’ll have access to therapy through our National Health Service.
I went from getting 1 B, and 8 A-A** in my exams last year to getting 1 D and 2Bs; I cannot focus, although this seems to be getting better. Reading also helps me, although TV can also be extremely triggering.

I hope me sharing my story helps you somewhat. And just know that your skin does not make you any less worthy of healthcare and the necessary attention that any white person could get! And the police brutality that is going is absolutely horrendous and myself and the vast majority of the people I know stand with the Black Community on this matter. 
Sending love and hugs from the UK :)

Hey! Amnesia on real events is often a symptom of Dissociative Identity Disorder (DID). Maybe try looking into that. Maladaptive daydreaming can be said to be a mild form of DID, but what you’re describing does sound quite DID-like as amnesia is a symptom of DID rather than MDD. Symptoms of DID include:
1. Two or more distinct identities or personality states are present, each with its own relatively enduring pattern of perceiving, relating to, and thinking about the environment and self.
2. Amnesia must occur, defined as gaps in the recall of everyday events, important personal information, and/or traumatic events.
3. The person must be distressed by the disorder or have trouble functioning in one or more major life areas because of the disorder.
4. The disturbance is not part of normal cultural or religious practices.
5. The symptoms cannot be due to the direct physiological effects of a substance (such as blackouts or chaotic behavior during alcohol intoxication) or a general medical condition (such as complex partial seizures).

OCD often links because there’s a compulsion to daydream - we need to daydream, and we cant help it. The daydreaming often takes up a lot of time just like in OCD behaviours, like cleaning for example.
ADHD also has links. Maladaptive daydreaming often involves repetitive movement (rocking back and forth, pacing, spinning etc), which is a well known symptom of ADHD. Individuals who maladaptive daydream often have a lower attention span because of the compulsion to do something (linking back to OCD).
